An independent integer coefficient expansion integrated these polynomials termwise, then specialized L=1 with normalized sides (1-x)/2,(1-y)/2,(x+y)/2. Both claimed moment identities had identically zero residual after clearing denominators (replay: node /workspace/checks/geometry-and-word-reproduction.js). Heron gives h=xyz>0 for x+y+z=1, and (4p-1-h)/8 is the normalized product of the three sides, so the reconstruction by Vieta is unique up to relabeling and congruence, including repeated roots. For the ratio minimum, AM–GM gives p>=(1+3h^(2/3))/4. The resulting lower bound for the numerator of Q-8/5 reduces to f(u)=1-28u^3/27+5u^5/81-2u^6/81 for u=3h^(1/3), strictly decreasing to zero at u=1, the equilateral point. For the upper bound, 27+27h-20p>0 since p<=1/3; the limiting value 12/5 follows as h tends to zero. At fixed h, M4 grows with p. The product level is the connected boundary of the compact convex superlevel set of log(xyz) in the simplex. At every extremum of the pairwise sum, the Lagrange equation makes each coordinate a root of one quadratic, hence two agree. The third, negative root of t^2(1-2t)=h lies between -1/6 and 0, so the positive roots sum to less than 2/3, giving 2t_+-3t_+^2>2t_--3t_-^2. This proves both endpoint orders and attainability of intermediate values, with the h=1/27 case forced by AM–GM. The theorem is exact with separately supplied L and positive area; no stability near degeneracy or conclusion for random-line chords is verified.
